title: Define how a requirement criterion will be verified
actor: A verification engineer preparing an assessment
goal: Make clear what observation would assess the selected criterion against an exact engineering state.
context: An engineering claim needs a defined assessment before evidence can be collected.
trigger: The engineer selects a requirement criterion and intended claim scope for verification.
preconditions: The requirement criterion and intended assessed subject are identifiable.

interaction.action: Supplies the criterion basis, exact subject state, selected technique, conditions, and expected observations.
Presents the verification definition and identifies any missing subject binding, condition, or criterion context.
Reviews the definition as the method to be performed, distinct from any future execution observations.

expected_outcome: A later assessor can understand the intended criterion, exact subject state, technique, conditions, and expected observations without mistaking the plan for evidence.

alternatives.condition: The appropriate technique is human inspection or review.
alternatives.outcome: The definition records its conditions and expected observations without requiring automated execution.

alternatives.condition: The criterion basis or intended assessed state changes before execution.
alternatives.outcome: The revised definition is attributable to its new basis and does not rewrite any earlier assessment basis.

failures.condition: The criterion, subject state, condition, or expected observation is missing or ambiguous.
failures.outcome: The system identifies the incomplete definition rather than implying that a complete assessment has been specified.

sources.basis: IR-004 owns the distinction between requirement, Verification, and Evidence; SR-025 derives the verification-definition obligations. Accepted as current requirement-analysis knowledge after independent coverage and clarity review: one owning IR and primary Feature, observable goal and interactions, classified outcomes, and applicable SR coverage. This confirms analysis only, not requirement approval, implementation, or satisfaction.
